how_to_use: cases: stored inputs exactly as the page imports or restores them; method: the specification both the driver and the reference were written against; expected: the independent reference values with their tolerances, decisions and corrections.

spec_changes.title: One filter rule for matrix cell, category jump and subject-field "Show"
An explicit supported ?lang= wins over the payload language
Self-check v10 derives the corpus size from the data

Element rules of the restore (page behaviour adopted): an element "" inside req or lift is dropped and listed with an empty value; a repeated lift subject is merged silently, a repeated req option is listed
Wording: languages cards_rendered counts the cards under the current filters (method.md 7.4 unchanged; text in cases.json corrected)
New graded outputs partial_link_notice and dropped_values on every URL case

conventions.steps: Each case is a list of steps applied in order to one browser page; method.md section 4 defines every step type and its effect on the page state.
conventions.viewport: 1440x900, fresh browser context per case (empty localStorage), browser language en-US
conventions.graded: Each graded key names one output; the comparison is exact (lists compared in the order stated, "sorted" lists sorted by JavaScript default string order).

cases.title: Record counts per type, as loaded and as rendered

graded.docs_total: number of document records the page holds after loading the data file
graded.key_conditions_total: number of key-condition (prov) records the page holds
graded.scenarios_total: number of scenario options offered in the scenario select (excluding the empty "choose" option)
graded.cards_rendered: number of document cards in the register list with no filter set
graded.cards_per_category: object {category: number of cards in that category group} with no filter set

cases.title: Coverage matrix: documents per subject area and category

graded.cells: object {area: {category: count}} for every area in AREAS and category in CATS, read from the matrix table (a cell showing "·" is 0)
graded.row_totals: object {area: total} read from the last column
graded.clickable_cells: sorted list of "area|category" strings for the cells that are clickable (non-zero)

cases.title: Document records validate against the schema

graded.violations: sorted list of strings "<record id>|<field>|<rule>" for every document-schema violation (rule names as in method.md 2.1); empty list if none

cases.title: Key-condition records validate against the schema

graded.violations: sorted list of strings "<record id>|<field>|<rule>" for every key-condition-schema violation (rule names as in method.md 2.2); empty list if none

cases.title: Scenario records validate against the schema

graded.violations: sorted list of strings "<scenario id>|<field>|<rule>" for every scenario-schema violation (rule names as in method.md 2.3); empty list if none

cases.title: Referential closure: key conditions point at existing documents and scenarios

graded.dangling_doc_refs: sorted list of "<prov id>|<doc id>" where a key condition names a document that has no card in the register
graded.dangling_scen_refs: sorted list of "<prov id>|<scenario id>" where a key condition names a scenario that is not offered in the scenario select
graded.prov_without_doc_or_scen: sorted list of prov ids that appear neither in any card nor in any scenario

cases.title: Referential closure: every area, domain, geography and category is carried by a record

graded.areas_without_record: sorted list of area keys whose matrix row total is 0
graded.domains_without_record: sorted list of domain keys for which the domain filter alone shows no card
graded.geographies_without_record: sorted list of geography keys for which the geography filter alone shows no card
graded.categories_without_record: sorted list of category keys for which the category filter alone shows no card

cases.title: Every document card renders exactly the key conditions that name it

graded.per_document: object {doc id: list of prov ids rendered inside that card, in display order (method.md 6.1)}

cases.title: The page's own consistency panel, each line evaluated independently

graded.flags: object {check id: true|false} for the listed checks, as defined in method.md section 9 (the page shows them in a hidden #val-out block; a passing line has class "ok")

cases.title: No catalogue key is echoed untranslated in any language

graded.echoed: object {lang: sorted list of catalogue keys that the page shows verbatim as text because the language lacks them}

# normenwijzer — method for the independent reference

This file specifies what `normenwijzer.html` (manifest revision `2026-10-15.normenwijzer-3`; the clauses changed in that revision are listed in section 11) shows for a given input, so that every graded output in `cases.json` can be recomputed without the page code. Sources, in order of precedence:

1. The page's own documentation: Learn texts and hints, shipped as catalogue strings in `normenwijzer-data.json` → `i18n.en` (keys named below), and the model equations the page writes into its calculation record (quoted in 5.1).
2. The vocabularies and the facet and scenario tables that sit in the page source as literal data. They are copied unchanged into `page_constants.json`.
3. Where 1 and 2 say nothing, the rule the code applies, written out in words. Each rule of this kind is marked **[code]**.

Section 10 lists the ambiguities.

## 1. Files and vocabularies

- `normenwijzer-data.json`: `docs` (document records), `prov` (key-condition records), and per language (`en uk de nl fr es pl`): `titles` {doc id: title}, `desc` {doc id: [scope, non-scope]}, `ptx` {prov id: [text, shape, conditions, check]}, `scn` {scenario id: {n: name, w: [6 reasons], b: [3 blind spots]}}, `i18n` {key: string}.
- `page_constants.json`: `LANGS`, `DEFAULT_LANG` (= en), `CATS` = [law, std, guide, method, rule] (also the display order), `STATUS`, `DOMS` (subject fields), `GEOS`, `AREAS` (subject areas), `FKEYS` = [proc, cont, req, ex, hygr, env], `FACETS`, `SUBJ`, `TPSUBJ`, `SCEN`, `LAYERS` = [chapter, openlaw, paidstd], `SRCFILES`, `BANNED`.
- `FACETS[i]` = {id, multi?, opts: [[option, expected subjects, not-expected subjects], …]}. Only `req` is multi-valued.
- `SCEN[i]` = {id, set: {proc, cont, req[], ex, hygr, env}, ar: [areas]}.
- `TPSUBJ` maps a key condition's field `tp` to the subjects that key condition belongs to.
- Catalogue lookup `T(k)` in language L: `i18n[L][k]` if present, else `i18n.en[k]`, else the key `k` itself (an "echo"). Titles, descriptions, key-condition texts and scenario texts fall back to `en` in the same way.

## 2. Record schema

A violation is written `"<record id>|<field>|<rule>"`. The graded value is the sorted list of all violations (JavaScript default sort, i.e. UTF-16 code-unit order). Identical strings appear once per occurrence (a record with two unknown areas yields two identical strings).

### 2.1 Document records (`docs`)

| field | rule name(s) | requirement |
|---|---|---|
| id, cat, st, geo, org, ar, dom, chk, fc | `missing` | the field is present |
| id | `duplicate` | no earlier record has the same id (each repeat after the first is a violation) |
| cat / st / geo | `enum` | value in CATS / STATUS / GEOS |
| ar, dom, chk | `empty` | non-empty array |
| ar / dom | `enum` | every element in AREAS / DOMS (one violation per bad element) |
| chk | `unknown_key` | `i18n.en["ck_"+element]` is a non-empty string (one per bad element) |
| fc | `unknown_key` | `i18n.en["fc_"+fc]` is a non-empty string |
| idn (optional) | `type` | if present, a non-empty string |
| `org.<L>` for every L | `unknown_key` | `i18n[L][org]` is a non-empty string |
| `titles.<L>` | `missing`, `digit` | non-empty string; contains no digit 0–9 |
| `desc.<L>` | `missing` | an array whose elements 0 and 1 are non-empty strings |

### 2.2 Key-condition records (`prov`)

| field | rule name(s) | requirement |
|---|---|---|
| id, ly, cat, st, tp, or, tr, wl, v, docs, scen | `missing` | present (ln, mt, tc, tcl are optional) |
| id | `duplicate` | as 2.1 |
| ly / cat / st | `enum` | in LAYERS / CATS / STATUS |
| tp | `enum` | a key of TPSUBJ |
| tp | `unknown_key` | `i18n.en[tp]` non-empty |
| or | `unknown_key` | `or` is "" or `i18n.en[or]` non-empty |
| wl | `enum` | 0 or 1 |
| v | `type` | array; each element is [string, string] (one per bad element) |
| v | `unknown_key` | the unit (second string) is "" or a non-empty `i18n.en` key |
| docs | `type` | array |
| scen | `empty` | non-empty array |
| docs | `figure_without_doc` | when `v` is non-empty, `docs` is non-empty |
| `ptx.<L>` | `missing` | `ptx[L][id]` is an array of exactly 4 non-empty strings |
| `ptx.<L>` | `claim` | no text contains any BANNED phrase after folding (7.1 `fold`) |
| v | `paid_figure` | when ly = paidstd: `v` is empty and no `ptx` text in any language contains a digit |
| tr | `untraced` | when the record "carries a figure" (non-empty `v`, or a digit in any `ptx` text of any language), `tr` is a non-empty string |
| tr / tc | `unknown_source` | when non-empty, the value is in SRCFILES |
| ln, mt, tcl | `no_place` | when `tr` is non-empty: `ln` is a positive integer and `mt` a non-empty string; when `tc` is also non-empty: `tcl` is a positive number |

### 2.3 Scenarios (`SCEN` + `scn`)

| field | rule name(s) | requirement |
|---|---|---|
| id | `duplicate` | as 2.1 |
| ar | `empty`, `enum` | non-empty; every element in AREAS |
| set.proc, set.cont, set.ex, set.hygr, set.env | `empty`, `enum` | a non-empty string that is an option of that facet |
| set.req | `empty`, `enum` | a non-empty array of options of `req` |
| set | `no_expected_subject` | under the scenario's own facets (5.1, no lift) at least one SUBJ subject has verdict +1 |
| ar | `not_expected` | no area of the scenario has verdict −1 under its own facets (one per such area) |
| `scn.<L>` | `missing` | `scn[L][id]` exists, and `n` and every element of `w` and `b` are non-empty strings |
| `scn.<L>` | `shape` | `w` has exactly 6 and `b` exactly 3 elements (checked before `missing` of the elements; when `shape` fails, nothing further is checked for that language) |
| `scn.<L>` | `digit` | no digit in `n`, `w` or `b` (checked only when `missing` passed) |

## 3. Referential closure

- A key condition names documents (`docs`) and scenarios (`scen`). A reference is dangling if the document has no record in `docs`, or the scenario no record in `SCEN`. Graded as `"<prov id>|<referenced id>"` (sorted).
- `prov_without_doc_or_scen`: key conditions none of whose `docs` resolves and none of whose `scen` resolves.
- `areas_without_record`: areas in AREAS that no document lists in `ar`. `domains_without_record`, `geographies_without_record` and `categories_without_record` are defined the same way over DOMS (`dom`), GEOS (`geo`) and CATS (`cat`).

## 4. The state, and what each input step does to it

The state has the fields: `lang`; `scen` (scenario id or ""); `dirty` (bool); `task` {proc, cont, ex, hygr, env: option or "", req: list}; `filt` {sec, cat, dom, geo, q} (each "" = no constraint); `lift` (a set of subjects).

Step types in `cases.json`:

- `{load: "normenwijzer.html?lang=X[&s=…]"}`: opens a fresh page (empty storage, browser language en-US).
  - Language: the first two letters of `lang`, lower-cased, if they name a language in LANGS (an *explicit* language); otherwise the browser language (en); otherwise en. An explicit language is never overridden by a permalink payload (8).
  - `data_transform` (optional, part of the case input): the page is served a modified copy of `normenwijzer-data.json`. `drop_docs`: the document records with these ids are removed from `docs` (nothing else changes). `append_copy_of`: a copy of each named document record, same id, is appended at the end of `docs`.
  - Default state: scen "", dirty false, every facet unset, req [], every filter "", lift empty.
  - With `s=`, see section 8.
- `{select: "#scen", value: v}`: lift is emptied, `scen` = v, `dirty` = false. `task` = a copy of `SCEN[v].set`, or every facet unset when v is "" (or unknown). Filters are not touched.
- `{select: "#f_sec"|"#f_cat"|"#f_dom"|"#f_geo", value: v}`: `filt.sec|cat|dom|geo` = v.
- `{type: "#f_q", value: v}`: `filt.q` = v, exactly as typed, blanks included.
- `{chip: {facet, option}}`: a click on a facet chip. For `req`: removes the option if it is in the list, otherwise appends it at the end. For the other facets: unsets the facet if the option is already chosen, otherwise sets it. After the click, `dirty` = (a scenario is chosen and at least one facet differs from its preset), with `req` compared as a set and the other facets by value. A chip toggled back to the preset therefore clears `dirty`.
- `{click: "filters_reset"}`: all five filters "".
- `{click: "task_clear"}`: every facet unset, req [], scen "", dirty false, lift emptied.
- `{click: "scen_restore"}`: the same as selecting the current scenario again (preset restored, dirty false, lift emptied).
- Navigation clicks into the register follow one rule: the click replaces all five filters, setting the ones it names and clearing the rest (search text and geography included).
  - `{click: "jump", cat: c}`: filt = {sec "", cat c, dom "", geo "", q ""}.
  - `{click: "godom", dom: d}`: the "Show" button of the subject-field row d in the task result: filt = {sec "", cat "", dom d, geo "", q ""}.
  - `{click: "matrix_cell", sec: a, cat: c}`: if the matrix cell (a, c) counts at least one document, filt = {sec a, cat c, dom "", geo "", q ""}. A zero cell is not clickable and nothing changes.
- `{click: "lift", facet: f}`: the "Show these anyway" button of the exclusion row of facet f (5.4). It adds that row's subjects to `lift`.
- `{click: "unlift"}`: the "back" button of the lifted row. It removes from `lift` the subjects that row lists (5.4).
- `{click: "kc_lift"}`: the "Show these anyway" button under a scenario's hidden key conditions. It adds to `lift` the subjects that hide them (6). If the button is absent, nothing happens.
- `{lang_switch: L}`: the toolbar language switch. `lang` = L and every other field is kept. Everything is redrawn in L, including the search matches, because the searched text depends on the language (7.1).
- `{permalink_roundtrip: true}`: section 8.

## 5. Task facets ("Describe the task")

Documentation (`i18n.en`): `fv_hint` — "A facet says one of three things: the requirement is expected, it is not expected, or nothing has been stated yet. The third is neither a quiet yes nor a quiet no." `ex_hint` — "A facet set to not expected takes the entries of that subject out of the selection. They stay listed here with the ground for it and can be brought back…". `task_hint`, `task_note`.

### 5.1 Model (the page's own record states these equations)

- `subjects(entry) = dom(entry) ∪ (ar(entry) ∩ SUBJ)`, in that order with duplicates dropped: first the `dom` list, then the areas of `ar` that are in SUBJ, in `ar` order.
- For the set of chosen options (a single facet contributes its option if set; `req` contributes every listed option): Y = the union of their expected-subject lists, N = the union of their not-expected-subject lists.
- `verdict(s)` = +1 if s ∈ N and s ∈ lift (lifted); −1 if s ∈ N; +1 if s ∈ Y; 0 otherwise. "−1 wins over +1 unless lifted."
- `selected` = entries with no subject at −1 and at least one at +1. `set aside` = entries with at least one subject at −1. Both are listed in data-file order of `docs`.
- An unset facet contributes nothing. If no facet is set, nothing is selected or set aside (message "none").

### 5.2 Facet marks

For each facet: `u` (Not determined) if it is unset. Otherwise `y` if at least one chosen option has a non-empty expected list. Otherwise `n` if at least one chosen option has a non-empty not-expected list. Lift does not change the marks.

### 5.3 The result block (`task_state`, `message`, `selected_count`, `domain_rows`)

- `task_state`: the pressed chips. `req` is listed in FACETS option order.
- `message`: "none" if no facet is set; "flat" if at least one facet is set and `selected` is empty; "result" otherwise.
- `selected_count` = |selected| when the message is "result", else null.
- `domain_rows`: only when the message is "result". The row "*" lists the categories (CATS order) with at least one selected entry. Then, for every subject field d in DOMS whose verdict is +1 (lifted included) and for which at least one selected entry has d in `dom`, there is a row d listing the categories with at least one such entry.

### 5.4 Exclusion block and card marks

- The ground of a not-expected subject s is a (facet, option) pair. Walk FACETS in order and each facet's options in table order; for every chosen option that lists s as not expected, record (facet, option). The last pair recorded wins **[code]**.
- For every set-aside entry, every one of its subjects at −1 is grouped under the facet of that subject's ground. `set_aside_groups[f]` = {subjects: the sorted subjects grouped under f, docs: the sorted entries contributing to them}. An entry can appear under several facets. Rows exist only for facets that have entries. The block is shown for both "flat" and "result".
- `set_aside_ids` = the sorted union of the docs of all rows.
- Lifted row: `lifted_subjects` = the sorted subjects in SUBJ that are in both lift and N. A lifted subject that is not in N under the current facets stays in `lift`, has no effect and is not listed. `unlift` removes only the listed subjects **[code]**.
- Card marks (the register cards, i.e. only cards that pass the register filters, section 7). They exist only when at least one facet is set. `card_marks_excluded` = the shown set-aside entries. `card_marks_lifted` = the shown selected entries with at least one subject in lift ∩ N.
- The task facets never filter the register. They only mark its cards.

## 6. Scenarios

Documentation: `scen_hint`, `scen_note`.

- Choosing a scenario sets the task as in 4. The six scenario cards (FKEYS order) each show a mark (5.2) and an "edited" tag. The tag is shown when the facet differs from the preset: for `req`, compare the sorted lists; for the others, compare the values. `modified` = scen non-empty and at least one card is marked edited (equivalently, `dirty`).
- `areas`: the scenario's `ar` in its stored order, each paired with `off` = (verdict of that area = −1 under the current state, lift included).
- Key conditions of a scenario: every `prov` record whose `scen` contains the id. A key condition is hidden when any subject in `TPSUBJ[tp]` has verdict −1 (lift included). `kc_shown` lists the remaining ones in display order. `kc_hidden_count` is the number hidden (0 when none).
- Display order of key conditions (scenario block and document cards alike): grouped by layer in LAYERS order (chapter, openlaw, paidstd), and within a layer in `prov` data-file order.
- `kc_lift` adds to lift every subject that hides at least one of the scenario's key conditions: for each hidden key condition, the first subject of `TPSUBJ[tp]` at −1 **[code]**.
- With scen "": facet_cards {}, areas [], kc_shown [], kc_hidden_count 0.
- The task outputs of a scenario case (selected, set aside, …) follow section 5 with the preset as the task.

### 6.1 Key conditions on document cards

Each card lists every `prov` record whose `docs` contains the card's id, in the display order above. These are never hidden by the facets **[code]**.

## 7. Register filters

Documentation: `reg_hint` — "Entries are grouped by category and never mixed." The record equation: "register shown = { entry : section, category, domain and geography filters all match AND every search token (or its stem, cut by one or two letters) occurs in id + number + title + issuing body }".

- `sec`: the entry's `ar` contains it. `cat`: the entry's `cat` equals it. `dom`: the entry's `dom` contains it. `geo`: the entry's `geo` equals it. An empty value does not constrain. All the conditions are combined with AND.
- Display: categories in CATS order. A group head is shown for each category that has at least one shown entry. Within a category, entries keep the data-file order of `docs` (so N07, a standard listed among the laws in the file, comes first among the standards). If nothing is shown, the "no entry matches" message is shown (`empty_message` true, `group_heads` []).

### 7.1 Text search

- `fold(s)`: lower-case (Unicode default lower-casing), then Unicode NFD, then remove the code points U+0300–U+036F.
- Haystack of an entry, in the current language L: `fold` of the space-joined list [id, idn or "", title in L (falling back to en), title in en, T(org) in L, `i18n.en[org]`]. Nothing else is searched: no descriptions, areas, geography or key conditions.
- The query: `fold(q)`, leading and trailing whitespace removed (JavaScript `\s`), then split on runs of whitespace. An empty query matches everything.
- Each token t must match. Its candidates are t; also t minus its last character if t has at least 4 characters; also t minus its last 2 characters if t has at least 6. Lengths are counted in UTF-16 code units after folding. A candidate counts only if it has at least 2 characters, and it matches if it occurs as a substring of the haystack. One matching candidate is enough for the token. All tokens are combined with AND.
- So a one-character query matches nothing, and "iso" also matches "isolated".

### 7.2 Matrix

`cells[a][c]` = the number of entries with `cat` = c whose `ar` contains a. `row_totals[a]` = the sum over the categories (an entry with several areas is counted once in each of its rows). A cell is clickable exactly when it is non-zero.

### 7.3 Untranslated keys

`echoed[L]` = the sorted catalogue keys k for which T(k) would return k itself (absent from both `i18n[L]` and `i18n.en`), among the keys the page displays: every key of `i18n.en`, every `org`, `"ck_"+chk`, `"fc_"+fc`, every key-condition `tp`, non-empty `or` and non-empty unit.

### 7.4 Language outputs

- `html_lang` = `page_lang` = the resolved language (4 and 8). `title` = T("ttl").
- `filter_labels`: f_sec T("l_fsec"), f_cat T("l_fcat"), f_dom T("l_fdom"), f_geo T("l_fgeo"), f_q T("l_fq"), scen T("l_scen").
- `category_options`: ["", T("f_all")] followed by [c, T("cat_"+c)] for c in CATS.
- `scenario_option_order`: SCEN sorted by its name `scn[L][id].n` (falling back to en), using JavaScript string comparison (`<`, UTF-16 code-unit order, no locale collation). Ties keep SCEN order.
- `cards_rendered`: the number of shown entries (section 7, current filters). `first_card_heading`: the heading of the first shown card, `idn + " — " + title(L)` when `idn` exists, else `title(L)`. The separator is space, U+2014, space.

## 8. Permalinks

- The link is `<site base>normenwijzer.html?lang=<current language>&s=<payload>`.
- The payload is the JSON (no whitespace, key order as below) of `{v:1, lang, scen, dirty: 0|1, task: {proc, cont, ex, hygr, env, req}, filt: {sec, cat, dom, geo, q}, lift: [subjects in insertion order]}`.
- Encoding: UTF-8 bytes of that JSON, raw DEFLATE (RFC 1951, no zlib header), then base64url without padding, prefixed with "D". If the deflated form is not shorter than the plain bytes, the payload is instead "J" + base64url of the plain bytes. Decoding accepts either tag. Without a tag letter, the whole string is taken as base64url.
- Opening a link: the language is first resolved from `lang=` (4). The payload is then decoded. If decoding or JSON parsing fails, the page keeps its default state and shows the notice "The shared link could not be read…" (`bad_link_notice` true). Otherwise every value is checked against the vocabularies; an unknown value is dropped and the restored state is:
  - `lang`: the explicit URL language (4) if there is one; otherwise the payload's `lang` if it is in LANGS; otherwise the language resolved in 4.
  - `scen`: kept if it is a known scenario id.
  - `task`: each single facet is kept if it is a string that is an option of that facet. `req` must be a list; each element is kept if it is a `req` option not already kept (first occurrence wins, stored order kept).
  - `filt`: `sec` must be in AREAS, `cat` in CATS, `dom` in DOMS, `geo` in GEOS; `q` must be a string (any text).
  - `lift`: must be a list; each element is kept if it is in SUBJ. A repeat of a kept subject is merged silently and is not listed (unlike `req`, where a repeat is a dropped value).
  - `dirty`: recomputed as in 4 (`chip`) from the restored scenario and facets; the payload's `dirty` is ignored.
  - Dropped, i.e. not kept: every value that fails its check. A missing field, a field equal to "" and an empty list are never dropped. Inside `req` and `lift` every element is checked on its own; an element "" fails its check and is listed with an empty value (`task.req=`, `lift=`). A `lang` that fails is dropped even when an explicit URL language makes it irrelevant.
- Partial-read notice: when at least one value was dropped, the page shows the notice "The shared link could not be fully read…" in the applied language (`partial_link_notice` true), followed by the dropped values as `field=value` strings joined by ", " (`dropped_values`). The field names are `lang`, `scen`, `task.<facet>`, `task.req`, `lift`, `filt.<field>`; the order is lang, scen, task in FKEYS order (each `req` element in payload order), lift in payload order, filt in the order sec, cat, dom, geo, q. A string value is written as is; any other value as its JSON text (`3`, `null`, `["a"]`). A `req` or `lift` that is not a list is one dropped value under that field name.
- `restored_state` reports `dirty` as 0/1 and `lift` sorted.

1. Resolved in revision 2026-10-15 (R1): permalink values are validated.

8. **Scenario sort order.** The order is the plain code-unit comparison, not locale collation. In uk and pl this differs from a dictionary order.
9. **Lift persistence.** A lifted subject stays in the state after the facets change and takes effect again whenever a later facet value marks it not expected (until "Clear selection", a scenario choice or `scen_restore`). The documentation only says entries "can be brought back".
10. **Duplicate violation strings in 2.x** are kept as separate list items. Every violation list in the current corpus is expected to be short or empty, so this only matters if the corpus changes.
